1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nxd4.strategy: Recaptures with the queen, which lands on the central d4 square where nothing can easily chase it, since Black has traded away the knight that would have hit it. White gets an active queen and the more comfortable game.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nxd4.name: Scotch Game: Lolli Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nxd4.background: The Lolli Variation, 3...Nxd4, was popular in the nineteenth century and received five columns of analysis in Freeborough and Ranken's 1896 manual Chess Openings Ancient and Modern.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nxd4.strategy: Takes e5 and c5 away from the queen and frees the c8 bishop, a solid way to catch up in development. White keeps at most a small edge in activity.
